title: Column lineage breaks on chained PIVOT and UNPIVOT
body:
SELECT id, score, headcount
    FROM sales UNPIVOT(score FOR month IN (jan, feb)) UNPIVOT(headcount FOR region IN (north, south))

Lineage only handles one pivot operator per source, so `score` and `headcount`
are traced to the wrong columns. Each operator consumes the previous one's
output, and lineage has to follow the whole chain.

title: Oracle rejects the PIVOT and UNPIVOT sqlglot generates
body:
Oracle only accepts plain column names in a pivot's `FOR` clause and `IN` list
(ORA-01748) and rejects `AS` before the operator's alias (ORA-03048):

    SELECT * FROM t UNPIVOT(revenue FOR month IN (t.jan, t.feb)) AS u

should generate `SELECT * FROM t UNPIVOT(revenue FOR month IN (jan, feb)) u` for
Oracle. The aggregate inside a PIVOT may stay qualified.

tests/dialects/test_oracle.py::TestOracl: [SELECT * FROM t PIVOT(SUM(t.val) FOR t.cat IN ('a' AS a)) AS p -> oracle]
[SELECT * FROM t UNPIVOT(revenue FOR month IN (t.jan, t.feb)) AS u -> oracle]

title: Dropping an unnamed UNIQUE constraint breaks the CREATE TABLE
body:
Spark, Hive and Databricks have no UNIQUE constraints, so they are removed when
transpiling. For an unnamed one,

    CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b STRING, UNIQUE (a))

should become `CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b STRING)` for Spark, Spark2, Hive and
Databricks, while DuckDB keeps the constraint. The output is wrong today.

tests/dialects/test_spark.py::TestSpark:: [CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b STRING, UNIQUE (a)) -> databricks]
[CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b STRING, UNIQUE (a)) -> hive]
[CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b STRING, UNIQUE (a)) -> materialize]
[CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b STRING, UNIQUE (a)) -> spark2]
[CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b STRING, UNIQUE (a)) -> spark]
tests/test_transforms.py::TestTransforms: [CREATE TABLE t (a INT, UNIQUE (a), PRIMARY KEY (a), FOREIGN KEY (a) REFERENCES u (b))]
[CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b INT, UNIQUE (a))]
[CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b INT, UNIQUE (a), UNIQUE (b))]

title: Support INSERT ... REPLACE USING
body:
Databricks supports

    INSERT INTO target REPLACE USING (c1, c2) SELECT c1, c2 FROM source

It should parse and generate back unchanged.

title: SingleStore: NULL ordering inside percentile WITHIN GROUP
body:
Percentile functions ignore NULLs, so a `NULLS FIRST` / `NULLS LAST` inside
`WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...)` changes nothing. Transpiling `PERCENTILE_CONT` and
`PERCENTILE_DISC` between Postgres and SingleStore should treat
`ORDER BY x` and SingleStore's `ORDER BY x NULLS LAST` as the same thing, with and
without an `OVER` clause.

tests/dialects/test_singlestore.py::Test: [postgres -> SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) FROM t]
[postgres -> SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(1) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) FROM t ORDER BY x NULLS LAST]
[postgres -> SELECT PERCENTILE_DISC(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) FROM t]
[singlestore -> SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x DESC NULLS FIRST) OVER (PARTITION BY g) FROM t]
[singlestore -> SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) FROM t]
[singlestore -> SELECT PERCENTILE_DISC(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x DESC NULLS FIRST) OVER (PARTITION BY g) FROM t]
[singlestore -> SELECT PERCENTILE_DISC(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) FROM t]

title: SQLite: DATE_ADD with a computed amount generates a broken modifier
body:
From DuckDB,

    SELECT DATE_ADD(d, INTERVAL (n) DAY) FROM t

should become `SELECT DATE(d, (n) || ' DAY') FROM t` in SQLite, and
`INTERVAL (-1) DAY` should become `'-1 DAY'`. Today the amount is not evaluated,
so the modifier SQLite receives is not a valid one.

title: Doris: reserved words are generated unquoted
body:
Doris 4.1 reserves words such as `analyzer`, `asof`, `both`, `char_filter`,
`dump`, `layout` and `leading`. An identifier with one of these names must be
quoted when generating Doris SQL, or Doris rejects the statement.

title: normalize_identifiers folds names it should leave alone
body:
Two problems with `normalize_identifiers`:

* DuckDB, Postgres, BigQuery, Redshift and SQLite only fold ASCII letters:
  `SELECT "FoÄ" FROM "BaÜ"` in DuckDB normalizes to `SELECT "foÄ" FROM "baÜ"`.
  Spark folds Unicode too.
* A dot into a semi-structured value (a MAP, VARIANT or JSON column) is a
  case-sensitive lookup into the data, not a reference: in
  `SELECT m.Foo FROM t` with `m` a MAP, `Foo` must keep its case, while a STRUCT
  field is folded like any identifier.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [SELECT ('{"Foo":1}'::JSON).Foo]
[SELECT ('{"Foo":{"Bar":{"Baz":1}}}'::JSON).Foo.Bar.Baz]
[SELECT PARSE_JSON('{"Foo":1}').Foo]
[SELECT PARSE_JSON('{"Foo":{"Bar":1}}').Foo.Bar]
[SELECT m.Foo FROM t]
[SELECT t.m.Foo FROM t]
[SELECT v.Foo FROM t]
[bigquery only normalizes ascii characters]
[duckdb only normalizes ascii characters]
[postgres only normalizes ascii characters]
[redshift only normalizes ascii characters]
[sqlite only normalizes ascii characters]

title: The Python executor ignores DISTINCT inside aggregates
body:
`sqlglot.executor.execute` computes `COUNT(DISTINCT v)` and `SUM(DISTINCT v)` as
if the `DISTINCT` were not there. Over the rows v = 1, 1, 2, NULL:

    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT v) AS c FROM t   -- expected 2
    SELECT SUM(DISTINCT v) AS c FROM t     -- expected 3

and the same per group under `GROUP BY`.

tests/test_executor.py::TestExecutor::te: [SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT v) AS c FROM t]
[SELECT SUM(DISTINCT v) AS c FROM t]
[SELECT a, COUNT(DISTINCT v) AS c FROM t GROUP BY a]

title: An expression's hash is stale after append()
body:
expr = parse_one("SELECT a")
    hash(expr)
    expr.append("expressions", exp.column("b"))
    hash(expr) == hash(parse_one("SELECT a, b"))   # False

`set()` invalidates the cached hash up the parent chain; `append()` does not, so
hashing and equality can return stale results.

title: Pipe syntax: generated __tmp CTEs collide with outer CTEs
body:
WITH x AS (SELECT 1 AS x1) FROM x |> SELECT x1 AS a |> SELECT a AS b

should become `WITH x AS (SELECT 1 AS x1), __tmp1 AS (SELECT x1 AS a FROM x),
__tmp2 AS (SELECT a AS b FROM __tmp1) SELECT * FROM __tmp2`. Today the CTEs the pipe
operators generate replace or clash with the outer ones.

title: StarRocks: parse REFRESH EXTERNAL TABLE
body:
REFRESH EXTERNAL TABLE hive_catalog.hive_db.hive_table
    REFRESH EXTERNAL TABLE hudi1 PARTITION('date=2022-12-20', 'date=2022-12-21')

should round-trip in StarRocks.

title: optimize_joins rewrites joins it cannot reorder safely
body:
`optimize_joins` moves conditions in joins whose meaning depends on them staying
put:

    SELECT * FROM x CROSS JOIN y JOIN z ON x.a = z.a OR y.a = x.a
    SELECT * FROM x CROSS JOIN y ANTI JOIN z ON x.a = z.a AND y.a = x.a

must come out unchanged, as must the `SEMI JOIN` forms.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [15, SELECT * FROM x CROSS JOIN y ANTI JOIN z ON x.a = z.a AND y.a = x.a]
[16, SELECT * FROM x CROSS JOIN y JOIN z ON x.a = z.a OR y.a = x.a]
[17, SELECT * FROM x CROSS JOIN y SEMI JOIN z ON x.a = z.a OR y.a = x.a]

title: Decorrelating EXISTS over a grouped subquery duplicates rows
body:
`unnest_subqueries` turns

    SELECT x.a FROM x WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM y WHERE y.a = x.a GROUP BY y.c)

into a join that is not unique on its key, so rows of `x` are repeated. The
rewrite has to group by the correlation key alone. Some shapes must not be
unnested at all -- a `HAVING`, a `QUALIFY`, a `ROLLUP` or an empty grouping set --
and an aggregate-only projection with `GROUP BY ALL` is always true. The
fixtures list each case.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [exists with a group by and having is not unnested]
[exists with a group by and qualify is not unnested]
[exists with a group by drops it so that the join stays unique on its keys]
[exists with a non-equality key and having is not unnested]
[exists with a rollup is not unnested since it returns a row even for empty input]
[exists with an aggregate projection and a group by is not always true]
[exists with an empty grouping set is not unnested]
[exists with an order by drops it]
[exists with distinct drops it]
[exists with group by all and only aggregate projections is always true]
[not exists with a group by]

title: MySQL: key parts of UNIQUE and INDEX pick up NULLS FIRST
body:
CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b INT, CONSTRAINT u UNIQUE (a, b))

should generate unchanged for MySQL, Postgres and DuckDB. An implicit
`NULLS FIRST` ends up on the key parts instead.

tests/dialects/test_mysql.py::TestMySQL:: [CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b INT, CONSTRAINT u UNIQUE (a, b)) -> duckdb]
[CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b INT, CONSTRAINT u UNIQUE (a, b)) -> postgres]

title: GROUPING() gets the wrong type in the Hive family
body:
`annotate_types` types `GROUPING(col)` as TINYINT for Spark and Databricks, which
is right, but Hive and Spark2 return BIGINT.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [1096, GROUPING(tbl.str_col)]
[1097, GROUPING(tbl.str_col)]

title: qualify_tables strips the parentheses of a function body
body:
In BigQuery,

    CREATE TEMPORARY FUNCTION f() RETURNS STRING AS ((((SELECT 'foo'))));

qualifies to a body without the parentheses the query needs. The result should
be `CREATE TEMPORARY FUNCTION c.db.f() RETURNS STRING AS ((SELECT 'foo'))`.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [Preserve wrapping parens of a query used as a function body]

title: Snowflake: PUT with an unquoted file:// source is not parsed as PUT
body:
PUT file:///dir/tmp.csv @%table

should parse to `exp.Put`, with the source as the string `'file:///dir/tmp.csv'`
and the stage as `@%table`, and generate `PUT 'file:///dir/tmp.csv' @%table`.
The quoted form already works.

title: Dremio: support the four-argument REGEXP_SPLIT
body:
Dremio's `REGEXP_SPLIT(string, pattern, mode, limit)` takes a mode such as `'ALL'`
before the limit.

    SELECT REGEXP_SPLIT(tags, ',', 'ALL', 1000) AS t

should parse with the mode and the limit in their own arguments and generate
them back in Dremio's order.

title: simplify changes the meaning of arithmetic when it collapses a CASE or IF
body:
When `simplify` reduces a `CASE` or `IF` with a constant condition to one of its
branches, the branch loses its grouping under the surrounding operator:

    x * CASE WHEN FALSE THEN NULL ELSE a - b END

should simplify to `x * (a - b)`, but the parentheses are lost. The same happens
for `IF(TRUE, a - b, c)`, for a branch that is `NOT p` under `||`, and so on.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [538, x * CASE WHEN FALSE THEN NULL ELSE a - b END]
[539, x * (CASE WHEN 1 IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE 1 - b END)]
[540, x - CASE WHEN TRUE THEN a + b ELSE c END]
[541, CASE WHEN FALSE THEN NULL ELSE a - b END * x]
[542, x / CASE WHEN FALSE THEN 1 ELSE a * b END]
[544, x * IF(TRUE, a - b, c)]
[545, x * IF(FALSE, c, a - b)]
[546, x * CASE WHEN TRUE THEN IF(FALSE, c, a - b) ELSE c END]
[547, CASE WHEN TRUE THEN NOT p ELSE FALSE END || 'x']
[548, IF(FALSE, FALSE, NOT p) || 'x']
[549, NOT CASE WHEN TRUE THEN a AND b ELSE c END]
[550, -CASE WHEN TRUE THEN a + b ELSE c END]

title: pushdown_projections prunes columns that a positional column list still names
body:
A column list on a derived table or CTE names the source's columns by position:
`WITH t(c, d) AS (SELECT a, b FROM x)`. `pushdown_projections` prunes projections
the list covers, which shifts every name after them. For example

    WITH RECURSIVE t(c, d) AS (SELECT a, b FROM x) SELECT c FROM t

must keep both projections of the CTE. The same holds for every operand of a set
operation under such a CTE, and for a source referenced twice with column lists
of different lengths.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [a source referenced with column lists of different lengths keeps the longest prefix]
[recursive cte column list applies to every set operation operand]
[recursive cte column list is kept by qualify, so its columns can't be pruned]
[SELECT t.c FROM ((SELECT a, b FROM x)) AS t(c, d)]
[SELECT t.c FROM (SELECT a, b FROM x UNION ALL SELECT b, c FROM y) AS t(c, d)]
[SELECT t.c FROM (SELECT a, b FROM x) AS t(c)]
[SELECT t.c FROM (SELECT a, b FROM x) AS t(c, d)]
[WITH t(c) AS (SELECT a, b FROM x UNION ALL BY NAME SELECT b, a FROM x) SELECT c FROM t]
[WITH t(c, d) AS (SELECT a, b FROM x) SELECT c FROM t]

title: pushdown_predicates loses precedence when it inlines an aliased expression
body:
Pushing a predicate into a subquery replaces an alias with the expression it
names, without parentheses:

    SELECT x.a FROM (SELECT x.a AS a, x.b OR x.c AS d FROM x) AS x WHERE x.d = FALSE

must push down `(x.b OR x.c) = FALSE`, not `x.b OR x.c = FALSE`. Arithmetic
(`x.b * 1`) and negations are affected the same way.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [6, SELECT x.a FROM (SELECT x.a AS a, x.b * 1 AS c FROM x) AS x WHERE x.c = 1]
[7, SELECT x.a FROM (SELECT x.a AS a, x.b * 1 AS c FROM x) AS x WHERE x.c = 1 or x.c = 2]
[8, SELECT x.a FROM (SELECT x.a AS a, x.b OR x.c AS d FROM x) AS x WHERE x.d = FALSE]
[9, SELECT x.a FROM (SELECT x.a AS a, x.b AND x.c AS d FROM x) AS x WHERE NOT x.d]

title: Spark: GROUPING SETS as a suffix and as a GROUP BY element are confused
body:
In Spark these mean different things:

    SELECT COUNT(1), d, h FROM t GROUP BY d, h GROUPING SETS ((d, h), (d))    -- suffix
    SELECT COUNT(1), d, h FROM t GROUP BY d, h, GROUPING SETS ((d, h), (d))   -- element

Both should parse to what they mean and round-trip exactly as written, in Spark
and in Hive.

tests/dialects/test_spark.py::TestSpark:: (sql="'SELECT COUNT(1), d, h FROM t GROUP BY d, h GROUPING SETS ((d, h), (d))'")

title: Transpile Spark's CONCAT_WS over arrays to Trino
body:
Spark's `CONCAT_WS` accepts array arguments, flattening them and skipping NULL
elements. Transpiled to Trino it should keep those semantics, for example

    CONCAT_WS('', ARRAY('a', 'b'))
    -> CONCAT_WS('', COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY['a', 'b'] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]))

The tests cover typed, untyped and mixed arguments.

tests/dialects/test_trino.py::TestTrino:: [spark -> SELECT CONCAT_WS('', COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY['a', 'b'] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]))] (source='"CONCAT_WS(\'\', ARRAY(\'a\', \'b\'))"')
[spark -> SELECT CONCAT_WS('-', COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY['a', NULL, '', 'b'] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]))] (source='"CONCAT_WS(\'-\', ARRAY(\'a\', NULL, \'\', \'b\'))"')
[spark -> SELECT CONCAT_WS('-', COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY[] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]))] (source='"CONCAT_WS(\'-\', ARRAY())"')
[spark -> SELECT CONCAT_WS('-', COALESCE(TRY_CAST(NULL AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]))] (source='"CONCAT_WS(\'-\', CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<STRING>))"')

[spark -> SELECT CONCAT_WS('-', CONCAT(ARRAY[CAST('x' AS VARCHAR)], COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY[] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]), COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY[NULL] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]), COALESCE(TRY_CAST(NULL AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]), ARRAY[CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR)], ARRAY[CAST('y' AS VARCHAR)]))] (source='"CONCAT_WS(\'-\', \'x\', ARRAY(), ARRAY(NULL), CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<STRING>), NULL, \'y\')"')
[spark -> SELECT CONCAT_WS('-', CONCAT(COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY['abc', 'def'] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]), ARRAY[CAST('ghi' AS VARCHAR)]))] (source='"CONCAT_WS(\'-\', ARRAY(\'abc\', \'def\'), \'ghi\')"')

[spark -> SELECT CONCAT_WS('-', CONCAT(COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY['abc', 'def'] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]), COALESCE(CAST(ARRAY['bla', 'bob'] AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[])))] (source='"CONCAT_WS(\'-\', ARRAY(\'abc\', \'def\'), ARRAY(\'bla\', \'bob\'))"')
[spark -> SELECT CONCAT_WS(NULL, COALESCE(TRY_CAST(NULL AS ARRAY(VARCHAR)), ARRAY[]))] (source="'CONCAT_WS(NULL, CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<STRING>))'")
(sql='"SELECT CONCAT_WS(\'-\', ARRAY(\'a\'), t.b) FROM t"', annotated='False')
(sql='"SELECT CONCAT_WS(\'-\', ARRAY(\'a\'), t.b) FROM t"', annotated='True')
(sql='"SELECT CONCAT_WS(\'-\', t.a, t.b) FROM t"', annotated='False')
(sql='"SELECT CONCAT_WS(\'-\', t.a, t.b) FROM t"', annotated='True')

title: Druid: JSON_VALUE with RETURNING
body:
SELECT JSON_VALUE(x, '$.a' RETURNING BIGINT) FROM t

should round-trip in Druid, with and without `RETURNING`.

title: The optimizer scopes subqueries inside DML and DDL wrongly
body:
Queries embedded in `MERGE`, `UPDATE`, `INSERT` and `CREATE TABLE AS` are scoped
as if they belonged to the statement around them. For example
`eliminate_subqueries` hoists a CTE out of an `UPDATE`'s value subquery:

    UPDATE t SET x = (SELECT a FROM (SELECT a FROM x) AS y)

should become `UPDATE t SET x = (WITH y AS (SELECT a FROM x) SELECT a FROM y AS y)`,
with the CTE inside that subquery. The references of the DML shell itself belong
to no scope. The tests go through each kind of statement.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [DML shell references live outside every scope, so the statement is left untouched]
[25, UPDATE t SET x = (SELECT a FROM (SELECT a FROM x) AS y)]
[26, WITH c AS (SELECT 1 AS y) UPDATE t SET x = 1 FROM (SELECT x FROM (SELECT x FROM t2) AS i) AS s]
[27, MERGE INTO t USING (SELECT id FROM (SELECT id FROM u) AS i) AS s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET x = 1]
(test)

title: simplify's gen() gives two different expressions the same key
body:
`sqlglot.optimizer.simplify.gen` writes names and literals without escaping them,
so their content can forge structure:

    gen(parse_one("v IN ('x'',''y')")) == gen(parse_one("v IN ('x', 'y')"))

is true, though one is a single literal and the other two. Quoted strings and
delimited identifiers must be escaped.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: (test)

title: A qualified star exclusion removes the column from every source
body:
SELECT * EXCEPT (y.b) FROM x AS x JOIN y AS y ON x.b = y.b

should expand to `SELECT x.a AS a, x.b AS b, y.c AS c ...`: only `y.b` is excluded.
Today `x.b` disappears too.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [164, SELECT * EXCEPT (y.b) FROM x AS x JOIN y AS y ON x.b = y.b]

title: ClickHouse: LAG and LEAD are generated as lagInFrame and leadInFrame
body:
`lagInFrame` and `leadInFrame` are relative to the window frame, not the
partition. Under ClickHouse's default frame they return the default value where
`LAG`/`LEAD` would return a row, so they are not the same function. ClickHouse
has native `lag` and `lead`; generate those.

tests/dialects/test_clickhouse.py::TestC: [oracle -> SELECT lag(salary, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) AS prev_sal FROM employees]
[oracle -> SELECT lead(salary, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) AS prev_sal FROM employees]

title: T-SQL: star over an UNPIVOT expands columns in the wrong order
body:
SQL Server returns an UNPIVOT's value column before its name column:
`SELECT * FROM t UNPIVOT(revenue FOR month IN (jan, feb)) AS u` returns
`(id, revenue, month)`. DuckDB, Snowflake, Oracle and Spark return it after.
Qualifying the star has to follow the source dialect's order, and carry it to
any target.

title: A second OFFSET silently replaces the first
body:
SELECT a FROM x OFFSET 1 LIMIT 2, 3

parses without complaint, and the `OFFSET 1` is lost. It should raise
`ParseError` with "Found multiple 'OFFSET' clauses. Line 1, Col: 30.", and under
`error_level=ErrorLevel.IGNORE` produce `SELECT a FROM x LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2`.

title: GROUP BY reorders CUBE, ROLLUP and GROUPING SETS
body:
SELECT c1, c2, c3, c4 FROM t GROUP BY c3, CUBE (c1, c2), c4

comes back with the `CUBE` moved to a different position. The relative order of
GROUP BY items must be preserved, for `ROLLUP` and `GROUPING SETS` too.

tests/dialects/test_spark.py::TestSpark:: (sql="'SELECT COUNT(1), d, h FROM t GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((d, h), (d))'")
(sql="'SELECT COUNT(1), d, h FROM t GROUP BY d, h, GROUPING SETS ((d, h), (d))'")
(sql="'SELECT a FROM t GROUP BY a, GROUPING SETS ((a)), GROUPING SETS ((a))'")

title: Exasol: transpile MySQL's SHOW DATABASES and SHOW SCHEMAS
body:
Exasol has no `SHOW DATABASES`. From MySQL, `SHOW DATABASES` and `SHOW SCHEMAS`
should transpile to `SELECT SCHEMA_NAME FROM SYS.EXA_SCHEMAS`.

title: Hive: support NAMED_STRUCT
body:
`named_struct(name1, val1, ...)` is a Hive built-in:

    SELECT named_struct('a', 1, 'b', 'x')

should transpile to `SELECT STRUCT(1 AS a, 'x' AS b)` for Spark and Databricks,
and `annotate_types` should know the struct's field types.

tests/test_optimizer.py::TestOptimizer::: [32, NAMED_STRUCT('col', 1)]
[33, NAMED_STRUCT('col', 1, 'row', 2.5)]
[34, NAMED_STRUCT('col', 1, 'nested', NAMED_STRUCT('inner', 'x'))]

title: FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY without a count becomes a bare LIMIT
body:
`FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY` selects one row. Dialects that write FETCH as LIMIT turn
it into a bare `LIMIT`, which is invalid SQL and does not parse again. It should
become `LIMIT 1` there, and stay `FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY` where FETCH is kept.

tests/dialects/test_dialect.py::TestDial: [SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> bigquery]
[SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> doris]
[SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> duckdb]
[SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> hive]
[SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> mysql]
[SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> redshift]
[SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> spark]
[SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> sqlite]
[SELECT * FROM t FETCH FIRST ROWS ONLY -> starrocks]

title: DuckDB: table alias misplaced next to time-travel syntax
body:
In DuckDB the alias comes before `AT (...)`:

    SELECT * FROM t1 AS a AT (VERSION => 3) JOIN t2 AS b AT (TIMESTAMP => NOW() - INTERVAL '1' WEEK) ON a.id = b.id

should round-trip, and Snowflake's `FROM t1 AT (TIMESTAMP => ...) AS a` should
transpile to DuckDB with the alias in DuckDB's position.
